q: 1. The length of the divergent cone in a venturimeter is _________ that of the convergent cone.
explain: The divergent cone is longer (angle of 5-7°) to prevent flow separation and minimize energy loss.

q: 2. The divergent portion of a venturimeter is made longer than convergent portion in order to
options: avoid the tendency of breaking away the stream of liquid
explain: A gradual expansion (longer length) ensures the flow stays attached to the walls, preventing turbulence and boundary layer separation.

q: 3. The coefficient of velocity is determined experimentally by using the relation
explain: Using the trajectory of the jet, where x is horizontal distance and y is vertical drop, this formula solves for actual velocity.

q: 4. A pipe of length more than double the diameter of orifice fitted externally or internally to the orifice is called a
explain: A mouthpiece is a short tube used to increase the discharge through an orifice.

q: 5. In a short cylindrical external mouthpiece, the vena contracta occurs at a distance _________ the diameter of the orifice from the outlet of orifice.
explain: For an external mouthpiece, the jet contracts to its minimum area at approximately 0.25d from the inlet.

q: 6. The coefficient of discharge for an external mouthpiece depends upon
explain: The length relative to diameter determines whether the mouthpiece runs full, affecting the Cd.

q: 7. The coefficient of discharge for an external mouthpiece is
explain: For an external cylindrical mouthpiece, the coefficient of discharge ($C_d$) is approximately 0.855, which is higher than a sharp-edged orifice due to the reduction in contraction.

q: 8. When an internal mouthpiece is running free, the discharge through the mouthpiece is ............
explain: For an internal mouthpiece running free, the theoretical coefficient of discharge is 0.5. Therefore, $Q = 0.5a\sqrt{2gH}$.

q: 9. The discharge over a right angled notch is ............
explain: For a V-notch (triangular notch), the discharge formula is $Q = \frac{8}{15} C_d \tan(\theta/2) \sqrt{2g} \cdot H^{5/2}$. For a right-angled notch, $\theta = 90°$, so $	an(45°) = 1$.

q: 10. The discharge over a rectangular notch is ............
explain: Based on the formula $Q =  rac{2}{3} C_d b \sqrt{2g} H^{3/2}$, discharge is directly proportional to the head raised to the power of 1.5.

q: 11. The discharge over a triangular notch is ............
explain: Based on the formula $Q =  rac{8}{15} C_d 	an(	heta/2) \sqrt{2g} H^{5/2}$, discharge is directly proportional to $H^{2.5}$.

q: 12. The error in discharge (dQ/Q) to the error in measurement of head (dH/H) over a rectangular notch is given by ............
explain: By differentiating $Q = kH^{3/2}$, we get $dQ/Q = 1.5 (dH/H)$.

q: 13. An error of 1% in measuring head over the crest of the notch (H) will produce an error of ............ in discharge over a rectangular notch.
explain: Using $dQ/Q = 1.5 (dH/H)$, a 1% error in head results in $1.5 	imes 1\% = 1.5\%$ error in discharge.

q: 14. An error of 1% in measuring head over the apex of the notch (H) will produce an error of ............ in discharge over a triangular notch.
explain: Using $dQ/Q = 2.5 (dH/H)$, a 1% error in head results in $2.5 	imes 1\% = 2.5\%$ error in discharge.

q: 15. The sheet of water flowing over a notch or a weir is known as ............
explain: The continuous sheet of water that overflows the weir or notch is technically called the 'nappe' or 'vein'.

q: 16. The top of the weir over which the water flows is known as ............
explain: The top edge or surface of a weir or notch over which the water flows is called the 'crest' or 'sill'.

q: 17. The Francis formula for the discharge over Cippoletti weir is ............
explain: The Cippoletti weir is designed to compensate for end contractions, simplifying the formula to $Q = 1.84 LH^{3/2}$.

q: 18. In a broad-crested weir, the discharge is maximum if the head of water on the downstream side of weir is ............ the head of water on the upstream side of weir.
explain: For maximum discharge over a broad-crested weir, the depth of water over the crest ($h$) should be $ rac{2}{3} H$.

q: 19. According to Chezy's formula, the discharge through an open channel is ............
explain: Chezy's formula for velocity is $v = C\sqrt{mi}$. Discharge $Q = Av$, so $Q = AC\sqrt{mi}$.

q: 20. A venturiflume is used to measure ............
options: pressure difference between two points in a channel
pressure difference between two points in a pipe
explain: A venturiflume is the open-channel equivalent of a venturi meter, used specifically to measure the discharge ($Q$).

q: 21. The coefficient of venturiflume, generally, lies between ............
explain: Venturiflumes are very efficient with minimal energy loss, so their coefficient of discharge ($C_d$) is typically between 0.95 and 1.0.

q: 22. In a venturimeter, the divergent cone is kept ...............
explain: The divergent cone is made longer with a smaller angle (5°-7°) to prevent flow separation and minimize energy loss due to eddy formation.

q: 23. Hydraulic coefficient of an orifice means the coefficient of ...............
explain: Hydraulic coefficients include Cv (velocity), Cc (contraction), and Cd (discharge), along with Cr (resistance).

q: 24. In a short cylindrical external mouthpiece, the venacontracta occurs at a distance from the outlet of orifice equal to ...............
options: one-fourth the diameter of the orifice
one-third the diameter of the orifice
tow-third the diameter of the orifice
explain: In an external mouthpiece, the vena contracta typically forms at a distance of about 0.5 to 0.67 times the diameter from the entrance.

q: 25. In an inclined position, a venturimeter records ...............
explain: A venturimeter is independent of orientation (horizontal, vertical, or inclined) because it measures the differential head (h), which remains constant for the same flow.

q: 26. An orifice is called a large orifice if water head, is ...............
options: twice the diameter of the orifice
thrice the diameter of the orifice
four times the diameter of the orifice
five times the diameter of the orifice
explain: An orifice is considered 'large' if the head of water is less than 5 times the depth or diameter of the orifice, as the velocity variation across the opening becomes significant.

q: 27. Discharge through a totally submerged orifice, is directly proportional to ...............
options: difference in elevation of water surfaces
square root of the difference in elevation of water surface
reciprocal of the area of the opening
explain: For a submerged orifice, the discharge $Q$ is given by $Q = C_d \cdot A \sqrt{2g(H_1 - H_2)}$, where $(H_1 - H_2)$ is the difference in liquid levels.

q: 28. The upper surface of the weir over which water flows, is known as ...............
explain: The 'sill' or 'crest' is the top edge of the weir over which water flows. The 'nappe' refers to the actual sheet of water flowing over it.

q: 29. The notch angle for maximum discharge over a triangular notch, is ...............
explain: A 90° V-notch (triangular notch) is standard for maximum efficiency and ease of calculation in water measurement.

q: 30. If H is height of the liquid above the sill, the effect of end contractions, according to Francis formula, is ...............
explain: Francis formula states that each end contraction reduces the effective length of the weir by $0.1H$.

q: 31. The discharge through an internal mouth piece is more if its length is ...............
explain: When the length is at least 3 times the diameter (running full), the mouthpiece acts like a short pipe, increasing the coefficient of discharge ($C_d$) to about 0.707.

q: 32. Pitot-tube is used to measure
explain: A Pitot tube is a primary instrument used to measure the local or point velocity of flow by converting kinetic energy into pressure energy at the stagnation point.

q: 33. The rate of flow through a venturimeter varies as
explain: The discharge formula for a venturimeter is Q = [Cd × A1 × A2 × √(2gh)] / √(A1² - A2²). Thus, Q is proportional to the square root of the head (√H).

q: 34. The rate of flow through a V-notch varies as
explain: For a triangular notch (V-notch), the discharge Q is proportional to H^(5/2), where H is the head over the notch.

q: 35. The range for co-efficient of discharge (Cd) for a venturimeter is
explain: Venturimeters are highly efficient with streamlined flow, leading to a very high coefficient of discharge, typically between 0.95 and 0.99.

q: 36. The ratio of actual discharge of a jet of water to its theoretical discharge is known as
explain: The Coefficient of Discharge (Cd) is defined as the ratio of Actual Discharge (Qact) to Theoretical Discharge (Qth).

q: 37. The velocity with which the water approaches a notch is called
explain: Velocity of approach is the average velocity of the liquid in the channel just upstream of the notch or weir.

q: 38. Francis's formula for a rectangular weir with end contraction suppressed is given as
explain: For a suppressed rectangular weir (where length L equals channel width), Francis's formula simplifies to Q = 1.84 L H^(3/2).

q: 39. A section of a channel is most efficient if the discharge through the channel is maximum for a given
options: slope of the bed of channel
explain: An efficient or economical section provides maximum discharge for a given area, resistance, and bed slope by minimizing the wetted perimeter.
